tts_summary:
Good morning. It's Thursday, October 1st, and the morning is dominated by earnings rather than macro tape action. Let's get right into it.

The big story is Accenture, and this one is genuinely impressive. The company posted fiscal fourth-quarter earnings per share of $3.29 against the Street's $3.20 estimate, but the real headline is the revenue beat — constant-currency growth came in at 7% versus the Street's forecast of just 3%. All three major geographies posted 7% growth. Bookings were massive at $22.2 billion, well above the $20 billion forecast, giving them a book-to-bill of 1.2 times. Managed services bookings were even stronger at 1.4 times. Looking into fiscal 2027, the company guides constant-currency revenue growth of 4.5% at the midpoint versus the Street's 3.8%, and EPS of $14.60, which is roughly inline with consensus — the modest shortfall there is purely a tax rate issue, not anything operational. Adam's bottom line: this is a sharp contrast to the disappointing June release and signals that enterprise demand, including AI-related work, is holding up well. This is a meaningful positive read-through for the broader IT services space.

Acuity Brands also delivered, posting fiscal fourth-quarter EPS of $5.77, up 11% and ahead of the Street's $5.56 estimate. Gross margins jumped 130 basis points, operating margins up 10 basis points, excluding tariff refunds. Revenue was right inline at $1.244 billion.

Cardinal Health announced it has extended its distribution agreement with CVS Health through June 2032. The company reaffirmed fiscal 2027 non-GAAP EPS growth of 13% to 15%, or $12.40 to $12.60, and maintained its long-term EPS growth guide of 12% to 14%. This removes a meaningful contract renewal overhang.

McCormick beat fiscal third-quarter EPS at 86 cents versus 76 cents expected, with organic revenue up 1.9% and strong margin expansion — adjusted gross margins up 180 basis points, operating margins up 70 basis points. The problem is the company left its full-year guidance unchanged despite the outperformance. Adam thinks general investor negativity toward food staples will cap any meaningful rally here.

On the macro side, the housing market is the cautionary note. Rising mortgage rates have effectively frozen buyer activity — one industry voice quoted today said buyers have hit a wall and are stepping back en masse. That's a persistent headwind for housing-adjacent names.

Directionally, the Accenture result is the dominant catalyst today and should support the IT services and consulting complex. The broader market tone depends on how investors weigh strong corporate execution against the ongoing rate-driven macro drag. Watch the IT services sector for follow-through, and keep an eye on housing-sensitive names which remain under pressure.
